title: Defining lipid droplet homeostasis in Alzheimer's disease and aging with high molecular specificity using mass spectrometry imaging and isomer resolved lipidomics
text:
The role of lipid homeostasis in aging and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is poorly understood, which is notable
because lipid droplets (LDs) were included in the very first histological descriptions of brain tissue from patients
with AD. We will produce the first high molecular specificity and high spatial resolution isomer-resolved
lipidomic survey of brain regions and cell types involved in LD dysregulation as it relates to normal aging and
AD. Using adaptive image fusion and machine learning methods, we will produce dense lipid fingerprints with
regional and cell type specificity that will be incorporated into existing atlases and will be available to the
community as a resource.

title: THE NIA GENETICS OF ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE DATA STORAGE SITE
text:
NIAGADS is an important NIA infrastructure for Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. NIAGADS
ensures high quality data and resources are available to the research community for AD
genetics research.

title: Probing parathyroid organogenesis to instruct stem cell differentiation strategies
text:
The promise of stem cell therapies has now existed for decades, but so far there are very few applications where
basic insights from developmental biology have successfully made it to the clinic. The proposed studies will you
a novel approach to determine key steps needed to turn stem cells into cells could be used to cure
hypoprathyroidism, a disease in which patients lack the ability to maintain healthy levels of calcium in their
bodies. To do this, I will test special molecules and short-term activation of key steps to guide stem cells toward
a parathyroid-like state to address this debilitating illness with limited therapeutic options.

title: Cell-resolution imaging of synapses and circuits in post-mortem specimens
text:
There is broad recognition that the anatomy of neural connectivity is key to nervous system function and
aberrant connectivity key to disease manifestations. Nevertheless, it is very often not possible to understand
exactly how, at the cellular level, normal brain circuitry functions and aberrant circuitry causes disease. Here
we describe the development of a strategy for visualizing brain connectivity using light microscopy that will be
applicable to specimens that are incompatible with the available genetic techniques.

title: An enabling approach for deep metaproteomic characterization ofmicrobial contributors to tumorigenesis in clinical samples
text:
It is known that microorganisms (e.g., bacteria) directly interact with human host cells and influence cancer
development, but we lack understanding of the molecular mechanisms through which these interactions happen.
We will develop a new approach, termed CS-BONCAT (cancer sample bio-orthogonal non-canonical amino acid
tagging) to more completely characterize the proteins expressed by bacteria found in cancer samples collected
in the clinic, providing a transformative method for understanding host-microorganism interactions in cancer.

title: Early Changes of T2* Measures in Lung Tissues using deltaTE-UTE MRI on healthy and COPD Patients
text:
Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a major global health concern, with rising prevalence and
significant impact on individuals and healthcare systems. The diagnosis and management of COPD face hurdles
owing to its often late detection and frequent underdiagnosis. To address this, our aim is to develop a rapid non-
contrast and non-ionizing MR imaging technique that can detect subtle early-stage changes in lung parenchyma
attributed to COPD, thereby improving our understanding of the disease and patient outcomes.

title: Computational and Biophysical Analysis of the Filovirus Matrix Protein System
text:
Public Health Narrative
Filoviruses including Ebola and Marburg Virus are among the most lethal infectious diseases and a potential
bioterrorism agent, but no FDA approved treatment options are available. Filoviruses contain only seven genes
with the most conserved of protein, matrix protein VP40, having multiple functions in viral assembly.
Identification of key VP40 protein conformational dynamics and regulation of VP40 assembly will elucidate
mechanisms by which VP40 fulfills its multiple roles and how they are affected by mutations, providing not only
the basis for rational drug development targeting this intricate mechanism but also providing biophysical
insights into protein-protein interactions involved in many other diseases.

title: Crowd-Powered Machine Learning to Diagnose ASD and ADHD in Adolescents from Digital Social Interactions
text:
Diagnostics for childhood and adolescent psychiatric conditions are inaccessible to many populations due to
long waiting lists, lack of health insurance, or the absence of proximity to the nearest available and affordable
clinician. Given the increasing ubiquity of Internet-enabled digital devices, computational diagnostics have the
potential to lower the access barriers to health care, paving the way for remote, scalable, and accessible
psychiatric evaluations. This project centers around the use of innovative crowdsourcing algorithms combined
with established machine learning feature extraction approaches to simultaneously predict diagnoses of Autism
Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), including potential comorbidities
between the two conditions, in a precise and specific manner.

title: Investigating the role of intercellular communication in synovial sarcoma progression using integrated nanopore sensing
text:
This project will develop a highly accurate and sensitive nanopore assay for the detection of RNA and protein
biomarkers in synovial sarcoma, a tumor that frequently affects adolescents and young adults. The innovative
nanopore technology will be used to study how the secretion of RNA and protein biomarkers drives synovial
sarcoma progression. The innovative nanopore technology developed in this project will also be applicable to
other cancers as well as autoimmune and neurodegenerative diseases.

title: The role of adverse social-biological interactions in acute myeloid leukemia disparities
text: Analyses from our real-world Chicago AML registry suggest that contextual features of the social and physical environment (SPE) can influence the molecular topography of leukemia thereby contributing to suboptimal survival AML in socially vulnerable populations. We hypothesize that social stressors result in innate immune system activation and an inflammatory microenvironment that are highly permissive to the growth of hematopoietic stem cells with p53 mutations. The population-based (Aim 1) and in vivo (Aim 2) studies of gene-environment interaction will provide insights into mechanisms whereby SPE can promote malignant hematopoiesis and validate the inflammasome as a therapeutic target to mitigate the impact of social adversity on AML survival .

title: Dissecting the cellular and spatial tissue clock of the human lung and peripheral blood
text:
This proposal seeks to better understand how age affects the cellular microenvironment of the lung and blood
using human samples, which has primarily been studied in mouse models to date and without the use of
single-cell resolution technologies. Our approach will combine single-cell transcriptomic data and age
information from hundreds of samples with spatially-resolved measurements of lung tissue organization and
machine learning to uncover and validate age-specific cell frequencies, gene expression programs, cell
interactions, spatially resolved multicellular communities, and therapeutic targets that can delay age-related
decline in lung function. Our computational methodology can be used to study the relationship between age
and the cellular microenvironment in other human tissues or organs.

title: Developing HIV Resistant Hematopoietic Stem Cells through Targeted Base Editing
text:
HIV infects human blood cells via the CD4 receptor and one of two co-receptors: CCR5 or CXCR4. Utilizing
gene editing tools on human blood stem cells to target CCR5 and CXCR4 can generate HIV resistant human
blood stem cells. These modified cells could serve as a potential new treatment option for HIV patients.

title: CORE 3 - Quantitative Metabolism and Imaging Core
text: The Quantitative Metabolism and Imaging Core will provide nutrition and obesity researchers access to advanced techniques to study metabolism. Core users will be provided targeted metabolomics, stable isotope tracer measurements of metabolic flux, and imaging approaches. The Core will also consult with investigators on experimental design and data interpretation. Metabolomic approaches will be used to quantify intermediary metabolites and co-factors in plasma or tissue extracts using targeted MS based metabolomics. Since these analyses can be performed quickly and inexpensively, they will be used as the first line of investigation to inform the design of more intensive flux experiments. Stable isotope tracer experiments will provide detailed information about the function of entire pathways by using labeled substrates that incorporate into downstream metabolites. Labeling characteristics of metabolites, detected by NMR and/or MS, will be used to determine metabolite turnover or perform metabolic flux analysis. Data will be returned to the investigator and core staff will be consulted on data interpretation. These approaches can be used in projects involving cell culture, mouse models and human subjects. Flux studies can be coordinated with additional analysis of body composition and tissue intracellular lipid content using in vivo imaging spectroscopy techniques. Additional metabolic imaging studies of tissue specific metabolic flux can be achieved using 13C- hyperpolarized imaging. The Quantitative Metabolism and Imaging Core provides access to many of the state- of-the-art approaches necessary for NORC investigators to carry out rigorous and innovative studies of nutrition and obesity research.

title: Economic Evaluation Core
text:
Core C (Economic Evaluation Core): NARRATIVE (Wilson and Kim)
The Economic Evaluation Core (Core C) will provide health economics expertise to aid the 2DETECT Projects
in conducting a comprehensive economic evaluation focused on the implementation of population-based
genetic testing of hereditary cancer syndromes for all demographic groups and analyzing benefits and costs of
such work. In addition, Core C will assist Core A in developing and implementing a tracking and evaluation
system to monitor and evaluate performance and integration across 2DETECT. Centralizing this support will
allow the Projects to determine cost-effective, integrative strategies for broad health system-level genetic
testing of hereditary cancer syndromes, thus fostering policy and clinical practice change.

title: Accessing and expanding microbial bioactive chemical diversity by synthetic biology and new enzymology
text:
The goal of the proposed research is to discover and produce bioactive natural products and analogs of less-
studied microbes by developing new research strategies. In so doing, the research will directly impact the
biomedical mission of the NIH by providing novel drug leads to address unmet medical needs.

title: Technology Development for Whole Brain Functional and Structural Connectivity Mapping at 10.5T
text:
In addition to advancing our understanding of how the human brain functions, functional and diffusion magnetic
resonance imaging (fMRI and dMRI) have shown tremendous potential in diagnosing and investigating
neurological and psychiatric disorders, including schizophrenia, Parkinson's disease, epilepsy, Alzheimer’s
disease, and multiple sclerosis. In this application, we propose cutting-edge technological developments and
proof-of-concept studies that aim to significantly enhance our capabilities for exploring the human brain using
fMRI and dMRI.

title: The role of endothelial ceramides in coronary atherosclerosis
text:
The proposed research is relevant to the public health because coronary artery disease is the major cause of
mortality in USA and the third worldwide, accounting for more than 17 million deaths. The sphingolipid ceramides
strongly correlate with coronary artery disease, but their pathological role remains poorly understood. In this
proposal, we will use clinically relevant animal models to explore novel pathophysiological mechanisms of
coronary artery disease and pave the way towars new therapeutic strategies.

title: Deciphering the role of chemical signals in inflammation with open microfluidic functional assays - Equipment Supplement
text:
Molecular communication across cell types is central to life—communication between cell types in a human
organ is critical to normal function, and microbe-host or microbe-microbe communication drives microbial
ecosystems. This proposal will study signaling between human immune cells and fibroblasts and signaling
between microbes relevant for human health (e.g., commensal and pathogenic bacteria and fungi). We will
develop a suite of microfluidic tools to broaden the scope of mechanistic questions that can be addressed,
ultimately enabling the development of therapies to target dysfunctional signaling and inflammation in human
disease.

title: Morphologic and Kinematic Adaptations of the Subtalar Joint after Ankle Fusion Surgery in Patients with Varus-type Ankle Osteoarthritis
text:
The results of this research will provide quantitative characterization of anatomical form and its relationship
with function in patients that undergo ankle fusion surgery to treat ankle osteoarthritis. These data should help
surgeons to better address deformities at the time of ankle fusion surgery, which could in turn improve clinical
outcomes and reduce the likelihood that patients will develop secondary subtalar arthritis later in life.

title: Computational toolkit for robust detection of genomic variation in human leukocyte antigen genes
text: HLA genes are key mediators of the immune response in humans and have been linked to several hundred autoimmune disorders, inflammatory conditions, infectious diseases, and neurological disorders that can have significant consequences for patients. Despite rapidly amassing sequencing data on millions of people, scientists are limited in their ability to gain clinically meaningful insights about the role of HLA genes in disease due to the lack of appropriate computational tools. We will address this gap by developing a robust and well-supported HLA analysis toolkit that can scale to millions of individuals, thereby enabling researchers to discover novel HLA-disease associations that will drive the development of new preventive and therapeutic approaches.
